verdict.rationale: The Lowenstein x Clerky partnership lets founders self-serve incorporate a Delaware C-corp and complete real tasks online (bylaws, director/officer appointments, founder stock issuance, 83(b) elections) via standardized documentation, which goes beyond static templates. However, this is a third-party platform (Clerky) integration rather than a Lowenstein-built tool, and evidence doesn't show broader self-serve document assembly beyond incorporation/post-incorporation setup. Missing for 10: first-party Lowenstein-branded document assembly tool, evidence of self-serve coverage beyond formation (e.g., financing docs, IP assignments, employment agreements), and independent/hands-on corroboration of the Clerky workflow's usability.
